exercises.title: Which family is it?
exercises.intro: We lend in three product families. Drop each loan into Residential 1-4, Multifamily 5+ or Commercial.

items.text: Maple Run: a $340,000 fix-and-flip loan on a single-family home in Columbus, Ohio
items.why: A single-family home is 1-4 units. Maple Run is our Residential running deal (RD-RES-01).

items.text: Cedar Court: a $5,140,000 value-add bridge on a 50-unit apartment property in North Carolina
items.why: 50 units is 5 or more, so it is Multifamily. Cedar Court is our Multifamily running deal (RD-MF-01).

items.text: Birchwood Plaza: a $3,520,000 bridge on a 70%-leased strip center in Indiana
items.why: Retail is Commercial. Birchwood Plaza is our Commercial running deal (RD-COM-01).

items.text: A DSCR rental loan on a duplex
items.why: A duplex has 2 units. DSCR rental loans are a Residential product, repaid by rent (T1).

items.text: A DSCR rental loan on a fourplex
items.why: Four units is still inside Residential 1-4. Multifamily starts at 5 units (T1).

items.text: A bridge loan on a 12-unit apartment building
items.why: 12 units is 5 or more. A value-add bridge is a Multifamily product (T1).

items.text: A construction and lease-up loan on a new 60-unit apartment building
items.why: Construction and lease-up of 5+ units is a Multifamily product (T1).

exercises.title: Headline check
exercises.intro: Recompute three market figures from their own inputs. Then compare each with the headline the source reports.
sources: T2 market snapshot (KBRA, 30 Jul 2026; Bank of America via HousingWire, 2026)

buildup.context: KBRA reports $5.5 billion of RTL securitization in 2025 and about $4.8 billion projected for 2026. About $3.5 billion of 2026 issuance is expected to be rated. KBRA says about 73% is rated and issuance falls 12%. Non-QM originations are projected at $175 billion in 2026, up from $108 billion in 2025. Market data checked 20 Nov 2026; recheck before use. Enter percentages to one decimal.

lines.label: Rated share of 2026 RTL issuance (rated ÷ total)
lines.hint: $3.5 billion ÷ $4.8 billion. KBRA's 'about 73%' is the same figure, rounded.

lines.label: Change in RTL issuance, 2025 to 2026 ((new − old) ÷ old)
lines.hint: ($4.8 billion − $5.5 billion) ÷ $5.5 billion. It is a fall, so the answer is negative. KBRA's 12% likely comes from unrounded figures.

exercises.title: Maple Run's funding chain
exercises.intro: Each step in a loan's funding chain has its own buyer, standards and risks. Put Maple Run's chain in order, from our loan to a non-QM securitization.

steps: We fund the $340,000 bridge loan to Harborline Holdings LLC
We hold the loan, or sell it into an RTL pool
In month 14 the borrower asks to refinance into a DSCR loan
The DSCR loan may end up in a non-QM securitization
order.why: The bridge loan comes first. It is held or sold while the house is renovated and leased. The DSCR refinance repays it in month 14. That new loan can then be pooled into a non-QM securitization. Each buyer along the way applies its own criteria (T3, buyer standards).
